After breakfast, you will head to Lake Guatavita and Zipaquirá. The day’s tour takes about 9 hours, including travel, and the route reaches an altitude of around 3,000 metres.

Your first stop is the town of Guatavita, near Bogotá. After a short walk around town, you will continue to Lake Guatavita. The lake sits in the crater of an extinct volcano at over 3,000 metres above sea level.

This lake is associated with the legend of El Dorado. According to the legend, Indigenous chiefs covered themselves in clay and gold dust, went out to the middle of the lake and threw gold objects into the water as offerings to the gods. Many searches for gold have taken place here, but the legend remains a legend. Mountains surround the lake, whose water is a vivid emerald green.

The lake is closed to visitors on Mondays.

After the visit and lunch by the lake, you will continue to Zipaquirá. You will see the main square and the old streets before descending into the famous underground Salt Cathedral.

The cathedral was carved out of salt at a depth of over 170 metres. Salt makes up around 75% of its walls. Inside, lighting illuminates carved figures. The cathedral has been considered one of Colombia’s main attractions since 2007, and services are held here on Sundays.

The complex is part of Parque de la Sal. Visitors can explore a chamber with a lake, a mineralogy museum, a cinema and souvenir shops.

After the visit, you will return to Bogotá. The drive from Zipaquirá to Bogotá takes around 1.5 hours. Lunch at a restaurant is included.
Bogotá – Medellín – El Peñón de Guatapé

Transfer to the airport and fly to Medellín.

On arrival, you will head to Guatapé. The famous El Peñón de Guatapé rock formation stands near the town. Its name is associated with two neighbouring towns, El Peñón and Guatapé.

The rock is estimated to be more than 70 million years old. It became widely known after the first ascent in 1954. The Indigenous people of the area considered the rock sacred.

In a Tahamí legend, a fish named Batolita saved the people from the wrath of the gods by leaping out of the river and turning into a giant rock.

After visiting the rock, you will head into the village of Guatapé, where you will have time to walk around and have lunch. You will then return to Medellín.
